title: Sparks from one fire
hookLine: as sparks fly from one fire and fall back into it, so beings come from the One (Akal Ustat 87)

cards: Late at night at a bonfire, somebody drops another log on, and the fire answers. A column of sparks goes up into the dark.
For a second each one is its own bright thing, drifting its own way, a little separate from the rest. Then they fade and fall, and the ones that land in the coals simply become fire again.
Kids watch this for a long time without being told to. The stanza right after yesterday's watches it too.

teach.b: Akal Ustat, the next stanza, in paraphrase. As from one fire countless sparks rise up, and, each apart for a while, fall back into the fire.
As from one heap of dust the particles fill the air, and settle back into the dust. As from one river countless waves rise, and the waves, being water, are all called water.
So from the One, the form of all the world, beings appear; they arise from it, and into it they all merge again. Three pictures, one teaching. The spark says: for a while you really are separate.
Bright, moving, your own path through the dark. The stanza doesn't pretend that away. The dust says: even the small, plain, unglamorous bits come from the same heap.
And the wave says the boldest thing: even while it's rising, a wave never stops being water. You don't have to wait for the end to belong to the One. You're made of it now.
One way Sikhs read it: this is the shape of a life.

teach.h: FROM THE ONE, BACK TO THE ONE.
teach.b: You come from the One, you live as a spark for a while, and you return. A few days ago, the ninth Guru's hymn ended with a person blending with the Lord like water into water.
Here his son sings something close, in images of his own. It finishes the thought of the last two days, too. One human race, the same light: here's why.
Everyone you meet is a spark off the same fire.

how: Sikhs sing this stanza of Akal Ustat in kirtan, and its images of sparks, dust and waves are used in katha to explain how all beings come from and return to the One.

games.q: what does “sparks from one fire” mean?
o: beings rise from the One and merge back into it
souls that drift apart and never return home
the sparks of anger that start every quarrel

games.q: three pictures, three lessons: tap the pairs.
p: small bits from the same heap
the fire, the heap, the river

s: in the stanza, the sparks stay apart from the fire forever
each is apart for a while, then falls back into the fire.
the stanza uses three pictures: fire, dust and a river
sparks from a fire, dust from a heap, waves from a river.
a wave stops being water while it rises
the stanza says the waves, being water, are all called water.

games.q: a spark rises from the fire and drifts off into the dark. where, says the stanza, does it end up?
games.why: the sparks, apart for a while, fall back into the fire. so beings come from the One and merge in it again.

practice: If it's safe, light a candle or open a video of a fire; if not, close your eyes and remember one.

Watch how the flame moves and never quite holds a shape, and let yourself be one spark from it, bright for a while, from the same fire. If you pray, rest in Waheguru on each breath out, and put out any real flame when you're done.

wordCard.voice: Sparks from one fire. Like sparks from a fire, dust from a heap, waves from a river, beings come from the One and merge in it again. Today's word.

orig.note: a spark or particle, the word the stanza uses for the sparks and the specks of dust.

carryVoice: Your line: sparks of one fire. A wave never stops being water. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Dasam Granth, Akal Ustat 87 (jaise ek ag te kanuka kot ag uthe ... jaise ek nad te tarang kot upjat hai)
Guru Granth Sahib, Sorath Mahala 9, Ang 633 (ends: blending with the Lord as water with water)
